title: Jamaican-Style Allspice and Thyme Jerk Sauce
description: Allspice and thyme lead this mild jerk-inspired sauce, with roasted pepper, ginger and a little dark molasses underneath.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: peeled roasted red bell pepper
ingredients.note: Plain home-roasted pepper with skin and seeds removed.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: ground ancho chile
ingredients.note: Use pure mild ancho, without added salt.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

steps.title: Wake the jerk spices
steps.text: Warm {oil}, {al}, {thy}, {an}, {ci} and {nut} over low heat for 30 seconds until the allspice is fragrant.

steps.title: Cook the sauce base
steps.text: Stir in {bell}, {ga}, {gi}, {ch}, {mo}, {cv} and {a}. Cover and simmer for 7–8 minutes.

steps.title: Blend the jerk sauce
steps.text: Off the heat, blend until the thyme and pepper disappear into a smooth sauce. Return to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over moist chicken or pork. For more heat, pass Scotch bonnet hot sauce at the table.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit the ancho and use 1 teaspoon cider vinegar. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 44 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 7.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.4 g fat, 0.7 g fiber, 98 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 40 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 6.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.4 g fat, 0.7 g fiber, 30 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
